transitionsNote: `kind` is the transition's name in the ONE catalog (lib/reel-config-base/transition-schema.ts) — what a config writes and what the editor's Kind dropdown offers. Every entry must have one: an entry without a kind is a presentation nothing can reach, which is exactly the state the six below were fixed out of. `options` lists the params the editor exposes as sub-options, which is the kind's schema shape minus kind/frames.

glitch.description: Digital distortion with RGB shift and scan lines
glitch.bestFor: Tech demos, edgy reveals, cyberpunk aesthetic

burn.description: Cloud-masked burn-through with a hot glowing edge; brand supplies the mask and glow colour
burn.bestFor: Organic reveals, warm brand moments, film-like cuts

pixelate.description: Digital mosaic dissolution with glitch artifacts

whipPan.description: Directional motion blur — fast camera move feel
whipPan.bestFor: Energetic cuts, camera movement, fast-paced reels

zoomThrough.description: Zoom out of outgoing, zoom into incoming — high energy
zoomThrough.bestFor: Dynamic transitions, product reveals, fast-cut edits

wipe.description: Directional sweep in a brand accent-slot colour (the key resolves via the theme's accentSlots)
wipe.bestFor: Brand-consistent wipes, political reels, directional reveals

gradientWipe.description: Feathered diagonal blend band sweeping corner to corner
gradientWipe.bestFor: Soft corner-to-corner reveals, calm brand moments

scanlineGlitch.description: Compressed CRT scanline + RGB shift — rhymes with outro stinger
scanlineGlitch.bestFor: Digital/tech aesthetic, modern edgy reels, retro-futurism

transitionAxisNote: What EVERY transition carries, whatever its kind, plus how a brand adds a kind of its own. Added in Phase 4 (Workstream 1); brand migration notes in docs/superpowers/phase4-migrations.md. The `transitions` map above lists CORE presentations only and is not a complete index of the catalog — `lib/reel-config-base/transition-schema.ts` is (19 kinds; `dissolve`, `fade`, `fade-coal`, `slide`, `flip`, `clock-wipe` and `iris` have no entry above).

frames.description: Length of the transition. Rendered by the editor's dedicated length field, not as a sub-option.

alignment.description: Where the transition sits relative to the cut. `center` splits it (floor before / ceil after) — the pre-Phase-4 behaviour, so omitting the field is byte-identical. `start` puts the whole transition AFTER the cut (the incoming clip carries it), `end` the whole transition BEFORE it. At a reel edge it CLAMPS: there is no cut to straddle.
alignment.decidedBy: transitionHandles / transitionAlignmentOf in lib/reel-config-base/transition-schema.ts, read by both lib/render/video-track-layout.ts and the editor's transitions lane

enabled.description: Per-node switch shared with the effect axis. `false` renders a hard cut and stops the boundary lending handle frames, while keeping the authored params in the config for the toggle back. Absent means enabled, so no baked literal changes.

brandRegistry.description: The sixth extension axis: a brand registers its own transition kinds in the theme, with zero core edits. Resolution is the same as every other axis (resolveRegistered) — brand wins, core's generic beneath, and a config-only registration does not mask the generic. Before this, kinds resolved through a module-private table in at-cut-transitions.tsx and adding a look meant editing three core files.

registrationKeys.render: (props: TransitionRenderProps) => ResolvedTransition | null — a {component, props} presentation or a two-input TransitionNode
registrationKeys.params: readonly ParamField[] — the SAME descriptor the effect axis and EditorMeta use (lib/reel-config-base/param-field.ts). This is the whole editor declaration: editorMetaFromTheme derives EditorMeta.transitionProps from it, so the kind becomes selectable and editable with no second copy.
registrationKeys.config: theme-level constants, read with transitionConfig(theme, kind)

editorEffects: the Kind picker offers the catalog UNION the registered kinds (transitionKindChoices)
a registered kind's controls compose with core's structural ones (transitionParamsFor), a declared field winning by prop in place
an unrecognised kind is displayed as itself and survives an edit untouched — it used to be coerced to `cut`

componentsNote: Stand-alone visual primitives a template can drop into a composition (lib/components). They are NOT the layered rendering contract: the renderers a brand registers, the accent palette and the placement vocabulary live in lib/theming (SegmentMedia, GenericTextOverlay, GenericWatermark), and the assembly in lib/render. The five legacy-theme components (AnimatedBackground, Label, LogoWatermark, SplitScreen, NarratorPiP) were retired with lib/theme/ and examples/hello-world.

MazeDecoration.description: Animated isometric grid decoration for video corners with wave animation

coreModulesNote: The core modules a brand's build/editor shell is assembled from (Phase 2: core owns the brand shell). Unlike `components`, these are not visual primitives — they are the wiring a template used to hand-copy: the <Composition> prop bundle, brand font loading, the webpack/vitest/tsconfig presets, and the reel editor host plus its Vite dev-server plugin. Brand-side usage and the migration from hand-written copies: docs/creating-templates.md and docs/superpowers/phase2-migrations.md.

layeredCompositionProps.description: The <Composition> prop bundle for a layered reel — calculateMetadata from meta.totalDurationMs, the 60-frame floor, and layeredDurationInFrames as the one definition of a reel's length. Spread it inline in Root.tsx; the editor's surgical Save matches the callee by source text

loadBrandFonts.description: Registers a brand's fonts and blocks rendering until they are ready, with the render-concurrency hardening (120s timeout, 2 retries) as the default. Pure normalisation half in lib/render/fonts.ts

applyToolkitWebpack.description: remotion.config.ts preset — the @video-toolkit/lib alias, the resolve.modules fix for @remotion/transitions, the zod$ single-instance pin resolved from the project root, and the toolkit/lib existence guard

createToolkitVitestConfig.description: vitest.config.ts preset — same aliases and zod dedupe as the webpack side, with extraTestInclude appending to the default src globs

toolkitTsconfigBase.description: The nine compilerOptions every brand tsconfig repeats. Declares no `paths` on purpose: TypeScript does not merge paths across extends, so every template must declare @video-toolkit/lib/* itself

mountEditorHost.description: The whole reel editor as one call — state, history, keyboard handling, preview Player, timeline toolbar, crop gestures, save/discard. A brand's .editor/main.tsx is this call plus its CSS import. EditorHost is exported separately for hosts managing their own React root

createEditorViteConfig.description: Factory for a brand's .editor/vite.config.mts — aliases, the zod pin, the @remotion/transitions re-resolver, and createEditorPlugin appended. Must be imported by RELATIVE path: it creates the alias, so it cannot be loaded through it

createEditorPlugin.description: Vite dev-server plugin backing the editor's /props, /save, /render, /project-state and /sources routes. The save target path is closed over templateRoot at config time, never read from the request

formatWithProjectPrettier.description: Default formatter for the editor's Save — resolves the project's own Prettier config, and degrades to writing unformatted source when Prettier is not installed

default.description: Clean, professional brand with orange accent

layered-minimal.description: Minimal layered reel — CompositionTheme + inline LayeredReel + LayeredReelComposition; renders from two committed images, no API keys
